UCLA · KOGAR RESEARCH GROUP

A motorized optic rotator

A custom mechanism and electronics for rotating an optic in a condensed matter research lab.

A compact mechanism for an optical setup

In UCLA’s Kogar Research Group, I developed a motorized optic rotator for our condensed matter research work. It needed to be lightweight and slim enough to fit into the existing optical setup, so packaging was a central part of the design.

Five to ten physical prototypes

I personally built and tested approximately five to ten prototypes. I revised the mechanism, added a shaft coupler, changed pulleys, and tested how those changes affected the assembly.

Fitting the mechanism into a limited space meant considering the motor, shaft connection, pulley arrangement, and optic mount together. I enjoyed this part of the process because it required taking the design off the screen and finding out what actually worked on the bench.

Electronics and fine adjustment

We created a custom PCB for the system and added a motor controller. We also added a sensor at the end of the motor to support finer adjustment of its position.

My research work included programming a motorized half-wave plate to respond to laser power fluctuations, reducing drift by 4.5%. The project brought together optical instrumentation, mechanical prototyping, electronics, and Python-based control.
